records.reason: The control experiment retests the upright-versus-inverted face suppression finding attributed to Jiang et al. (2007), and the Results report faster suppression for upright faces plus a direct replication Bayes factor comparison against Jiang et al. The only supplied shipped original is Hung et al. (2017), a distinct sound-shape mapping study; it does not represent Jiang et al. No prior adjudication file was available at the supplied path.
records.location: Methods, control experiment; Results, control experiment; References, Jiang et al. entry.
records.omission_quote: It is well-established in the CFS literature that upright faces break suppression faster than inverted faces (e.g., Jiang, Costello, & He, 2007; Stein, Sterzer, & Peelen, 2012), and replicating this effect would thus validate the presently employed paradigm.
records.identity_quote: Jiang, Y., Costello, P., & He, S. (2007). Processing of invisible stimuli: Advantage of upright faces and recognizable words in overcoming interocular suppression.
records.duplicate_quote: Can a Word Sound Like a Shape Before You Have Seen It? Sound-Shape Mapping Prior to Conscious Awareness
